testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: One air brake system with two sets of controls.
One air brake system for each side of the truck.
Two separate air brake systems with one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems with one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls. One system controls the rear axle brakes. The other system controls the front axle brakes.

questions.question: What does a suspension system have?

options.text: Pressurized water to support the load.
The ability to handle any weight.

questions.explanation: Suspension systems have weight capacity ratings set by the manufacturer.

questions.question: What is a problem with a cargo cover that flaps while driving?

options.text: It allows air to cool the cargo.

questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap in the wind. A flapping cover can tear loose and expose the cargo. It may also block your view or the view of other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Challenge the driver to a race.
Ignore the driver if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore the driver if you can.
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way if possible. Do not provoke them with eye contact or challenge them. Do not react to rude gestures.

questions.question: How should your vehicle be positioned when alley docking?

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
Straight within the parking space boundaries.
At an angle within the parking space boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight within the parking space boundaries.
questions.explanation: When alley docking, pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Back your vehicle straight into the alley. Park it in a straight position within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if used on the rear tires.
Yes, but only when carrying heavy loads.

questions.explanation: Never use wheels or rims that have been welded.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
questions.explanation: Follow posted speed limits in work zones. Slow down if road or weather conditions are poor. Slow down even more if workers are near the road.

questions.question: Is saving money the main reason for a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: The main reason for a pre-trip inspection is to keep you and other road users safe.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safe vehicle operation?
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Always do a routine inspection before driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about hydroplaning is true?

options.text: It rarely happens with large trucks.
It usually happens only at speeds above 65 mph.
It can happen with a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. You do not need a large amount of water for this to happen.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, what can you do?

options.text: Drive onto the shoulder if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive onto the shoulder if needed.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder may help you avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support a large vehicle.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can allow poisonous gas to enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. Poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: While driving, what should you do with your mirrors?

options.text: Use them only when changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. This helps you see traffic around you and spot problems with your own vehicle.

questions.question: When going down a long hill, how should you brake?

options.text: Use mostly brakes and downshift sometimes.

questions.explanation: On a downhill grade, use your engine to slow the truck first. Use your brakes only when you need extra stopping power or to stop.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems use alcohol?

options.text: To stop the brakes from squeaking.
To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
To prevent people from breathing the air.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to stop ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: A distracted driver usually:

options.text: Is aware of what is happening around them.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving causes slow perception, delayed decisions, and wrong actions. Avoid distracted drivers when you can.

questions.question: What is true about headlights?

options.text: They are not needed at night.
They provide better light than the sun.
Use high beams whenever it is safe and legal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use high beams whenever it is safe and legal.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights at night when it is safe and legal. But dim your lights to low beams when you are within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle to avoid blinding other drivers.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: This is normal and not a concern.
There is a problem with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a problem with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only if pressure gets too high. If it releases air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic repair it.

questions.question: When checking windshield wiper blades, they should be:
questions.explanation: Check your wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and that they are firmly attached.

questions.question: How does night driving compare to day driving?

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because hazards are harder to see in the dark.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, should you increase the space between your vehicle and the car ahead?
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the space ahead of your vehicle. This makes it easier for the other driver to pass. Going faster is not a good idea because they may just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Commercial vehicle weight and load rules differ by state. Which rule applies?

options.text: The rules of the state where your trip started apply.
The rules of the state where your vehicle is located apply.
The driver can choose which state's rules to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rules of the state where your vehicle is located apply.
questions.explanation: Rules for commercial vehicle loads vary by location. Always follow the rules of the state you are driving in.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating your large vehicle, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the space between you and the car ahead. Avoid sudden movements. Do not speed up because the other driver may just tailgate you at a higher speed. Do not flash your brake lights or turn on your taillights.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of death and injury in work zones. Slow down when driving through a work zone.

questions.question: What does ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) do?

options.text: Prevent the air compressor from overheating
Prevent the front brakes from being used on ice
Prevent the brakes from being used if downshifting would be more effective

questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Why is it a problem to have too little weight on the front axle?

options.text: It is important for smooth steering.
It is encouraged because front axles are usually weaker.

questions.explanation: Too little weight on the front axle makes it hard to steer your vehicle safely. Balance your cargo weight properly.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down gradually. Control your braking pressure to stop safely and smoothly.

questions.question: What should you do with your vehicle's gauges while driving?

options.text: Watch them for signs of trouble.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch them for signs of trouble.
questions.explanation: Watch your gauges while driving to see if there are any problems. Check that all gauges work properly before you start driving.

questions.question: If you turn to avoid a hazard, what should you do about braking?

options.text: Do not brake because it can lock the wheels.
Hold the brakes down until you pass the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake because it can lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning to avoid a hazard. Braking while turning can lock the wheels and cause you to skid.

questions.question: If a load is 10 feet long, what is the minimum number of tie-downs needed?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo must have at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin.

questions.question: When you pull over on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: Always use your four-way emergency flashers when you stop on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: Being aware of what is happening behind you while driving is:
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulders regularly. Knowing what is happening behind and to the sides of your vehicle is part of safe driving.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must be:

options.text: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.

questions.correctAnswerText: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
questions.explanation: You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident to get a hazardous materials endorsement. If you give up your U.S. citizenship, you will lose this endorsement.

questions.question: In very hot weather, air pressure in tires may decrease.
questions.explanation: Air pressure increases when it gets hot. In very hot weather, your tire pressure will likely go up. Stop regularly to check that your tires are safe and not at risk of blowing out or catching fire.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your bloodstream?
questions.explanation: Your body processes alcohol at a fixed rate. Coffee and other tricks cannot speed this up. The only way to sober up is to wait and let your body do it naturally.

questions.question: Cargo on flatbed trailers should be:
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers or trailers without sides, all cargo must be tied down. This prevents it from shifting or falling off during transport.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Air braking systems work very well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air braking systems work very well.
questions.explanation: Air brakes are an effective and safe way to stop large, heavy vehicles when they are maintained and used correctly.

questions.question: Heavy vibration can mean a tire is failing.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle thumps or vibrates heavily, a tire may have failed. Pull over safely and check your tires as soon as possible.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Protect the driver from cargo in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo in a crash.
questions.explanation: Header boards (also called "headache racks") protect the driver if cargo shifts forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use your turn signals.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals and check your mirrors when changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Not expecting delays on your drive
Keeping a safe distance from other vehicles
Keeping your hands on the wheel
Not making gestures at other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Not expecting delays on your drive
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, expect delays and plan extra time. Also keep a safe distance from other vehicles, avoid gesturing, and keep your hands on the wheel.

questions.question: Which of these surfaces is the most slippery?
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when the weather is warm enough to melt ice slightly. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: When checking your tires before a trip, what should you NOT look for?

options.text: Tires that do not match in size

questions.explanation: Check your tires for problems with air pressure, cuts or damage, and mismatched tire sizes.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a header board, it should:

options.text: Be strong enough to hold cargo
Light up when the engine starts

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo
questions.explanation: A header board should be secure, free of damage, and strong enough to hold cargo.

questions.question: When driving down a long hill, how should you brake?

options.text: Use mostly brakes and sometimes downshift
Downshift first, then use the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift first, then use the brakes
questions.explanation: On a long downhill slope, shift to a lower gear first, then use proper braking. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail. A lower gear uses engine power to help control your speed.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Create space in front of your vehicle so the tailgater can pass. Driving faster is not safe because the driver may continue tailgating you at the higher speed.

questions.question: A stopped bus is:

options.text: Not a concern if no passengers are visible
Should not be on the road
A concern whether or not you see passengers

questions.correctAnswerText: A concern whether or not you see passengers
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front of or behind it, and the bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Does not change how you apply the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change how you apply the brakes
questions.explanation: ABS prevents brakes from locking during hard braking. You should brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would without it. ABS does not necessarily shorten stopping distance.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheel lockup during hard braking and provides better control. However, it does not necessarily shorten stopping distance.
